title: Elder Nun Upasanā: Upasanā, cross the strong flood, The flood so hard to cross, Subject to the King of Death. Bear this last body, Having…
content:
Elder Nun Upasanā:

Upasanā, cross the strong flood,
The flood so hard to cross,
Subject to the King of Death.
Bear this last body,
Having conquered Māra and his army.

title: “Greed gives rise to misfortune, Greed stirs up the mind. Greed is the inner fear Born within people. People do not recognize That special kind…
content:
“Greed gives rise to misfortune,
Greed stirs up the mind.
Greed is the inner fear
Born within people.
People do not recognize
That special kind of greed.

The greedy person knows not what is good,
The greedy person sees not the Dhamma.
Blindness and darkness occur
Where greed dwells together.

One who has abandoned greed,
Not greedy for what is to be craved,
For him greed falls away
Like a drop of water from a lotus leaf.

Hatred gives rise to misfortune,
Hatred stirs up the mind.
Hatred is the inner fear
Born within people.
People do not recognize
That special kind of hatred.

The hateful person knows not what is good,
The hateful person sees not the Dhamma.
Blindness and darkness occur
Where hatred dwells together.

One who has abandoned hatred,
Not hating what is hateful,
For him hatred falls away
Like a palm fruit cut from its stalk.

Delusion gives rise to misfortune,
Delusion stirs up the mind.
Delusion is the inner fear
Born within people.
People do not recognize
That special kind of delusion.

The deluded person knows not what is good,
The deluded person sees not the Dhamma.
Blindness and darkness occur
Where delusion dwells together.

One who has abandoned delusion,
Not deluded about what is delusive,
That one dispels all darkness
Like the rising sun.”

title: “Monks, if one does not intend, does not plan, and has no tendency towards anything, there is no basis for the establishment of consciousness. When…
content: “Monks, if one does not intend, does not plan, and has no tendency towards anything, there is no basis for the establishment of consciousness. When there is no basis, consciousness does not become established. When consciousness is not established and does not grow, there is no production of future renewed existence. When there is no future renewed existence, future birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair cease. Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

title: “Furthermore, monks, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis, simply because of sensuality, taking up shields and weapons, donning…
content: “Furthermore, monks, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis, simply because of sensuality, taking up shields and weapons, donning quiver and bow, they charge into battle with freshly plastered ramparts, and arrows are hurled, swords are drawn. There they are pierced by arrows, struck by spears, drenched with boiling dung, crushed by stones, and their heads are cut off by swords. There they meet death or deadly suffering. Monks, such is the peril of sensuality, a mass of suffering visible here and now, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis – simply because of sensuality.”

title: “Monks, the arising, the continuation, the production, the manifestation of the eye is the arising of suffering, the continuation of disease, the manifestation of aging…
content: “Monks, the arising, the continuation, the production, the manifestation of the eye is the arising of suffering, the continuation of disease, the manifestation of aging and death. The arising … of the ear … of the nose … of the tongue … of the body … of the mind is the arising of suffering, the continuation of disease, the manifestation of aging and death. The cessation, the stilling, the ending of the eye is the cessation of suffering, the stilling of disease, the ending of aging and death. The cessation … of the ear … of the nose … of the tongue … of the body … of the mind is the cessation of suffering, the stilling of disease, the ending of aging and death.”

title: Hemavata: “Who here has crossed the flood? Who here has crossed the ocean? Without footing, without clinging — Who does not sink into the deep?”…
content:
Hemavata:
“Who here has crossed the flood?
Who here has crossed the ocean?
Without footing, without clinging —
Who does not sink into the deep?”

The Blessed One:
“One always virtuous, wise,
Well-concentrated, inwardly directed,
Mindful — crosses the flood so hard to cross.

One who has abandoned sense-desire perceptions,
Who has overcome all fetters,
Who has destroyed delight in existence —
Does not sink into the deep.”

title: “As rain seeps into a house with a faulty roof, So lust seeps into an undeveloped mind.” “As rain does not seep into a house…
content:
“As rain seeps into a house with a faulty roof,
So lust seeps into an undeveloped mind.”

“As rain does not seep into a house with a good roof,
So lust does not seep into a well-developed mind.”

title: (Calā): Having been born, one must die, Seeing suffering in birth, Fetters and afflictions — Therefore I do not delight in birth. The Buddha has…
content:
(Calā):
Having been born, one must die,
Seeing suffering in birth,
Fetters and afflictions —
Therefore I do not delight in birth.
The Buddha has taught the Dhamma
That leads beyond renewed existence,
Abolishing all suffering —
He has established me in truth.
Beings headed for the form realm,
Those aspiring to the formless realm,
If they do not know cessation,
They go to renewed existence.

title: “Monks, one who delights in form delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. Monks, one who delights…
content: “Monks, one who delights in form delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. Monks, one who delights in feeling … perception … formations … consciousness delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. And, monks, one who does not delight in form does not delight in suffering. One who does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering. One who does not delight in feeling … perception … formations … consciousness does not delight in suffering. One who does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering.”

title: “To what extent, Venerable Gotama, is the Dhamma visible here and now, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise?” -…
content: “To what extent, Venerable Gotama, is the Dhamma visible here and now, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise?” - “Brahmin, being infatuated by craving, overwhelmed, with mind obsessed, one plans for one’s own harm, plans for others’ harm, plans for the harm of both, and experiences mental suffering and mental distress. When craving is abandoned, one does not plan for one’s own harm, nor for others’ harm, nor for the harm of both, and does not experience mental suffering or mental distress. Being infatuated by craving, brahmin, overwhelmed, with mind obsessed, one engages in misconduct of body, misconduct of speech, misconduct of mind. When craving is abandoned, one does not engage in misconduct of body, speech, or mind. Being infatuated by craving, brahmin, overwhelmed, with mind obsessed, one does not know as it actually is one’s own benefit, nor the benefit of others, nor the benefit of both. When craving is abandoned, one knows as it actually is one’s own benefit, the benefit of others, and the benefit of both. Thus, brahmin, the Dhamma is visible here and now, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise.”
